narr: Deep monsoon moisture over northern Arizona and an area of low pressure moving over the area from the east brought more thunderstorms with heavy rain, flooding, and at least one funnel cloud. A mesoscale convective complex formed late in the day and kept thunderstorms going through the night and into the morning of July 25.
ev: Flood waters swept a vehicle away in a low water crossing on Camino Real near Rocky Knolls Road. The flood water was estimated to be 8 feet deep. The body of the driver was found several days later at the confluence with the Verde River.
A flash flood in The Little Colorado River covered the Highway 191 bridge in St Johns and made it impassable.
Flash flooding covered the roads (including Highway 160) with water, mud, and rocks near Tonalea and Cow Springs.
McClaws Road was close in Holbrooke due to the flash flooding of the Little Colorado River.
Water was flowing through a yard south-southeast of Concho.
Minor street flooding with some garages flooded in Wildwood Hills Mobile Home Park area of west Flagstaff.
Some roads in Cottonwood were impassable with flowing water.
Flash flooding was reported along Navajo Route 4 west of Pi��on Rodeo. The flood water was 6-12 inches deep.
River Valley Road and Herold Ranch Road on the southeast side of Flagstaff were flooded and impassable.
The Agua Fria river gauge near Dewey-Humboldt measured a 6.5 foot rise around 1800 on July 24. The river gauge near Cordes Junction reported a 6.7 foot rise around 240 AM on July 25..
